title: NumHTML: Numeric-Oriented Hierarchical Transformer Model for Multi-Task Financial Forecasting
target_asset: financial numerals in earnings conference call data
asset_universe: S&P 500 companies in U.S. stock exchanges
horizon: list maximum from 5 numbers; no time-based forecast horizon
label_definition: Given a list of 5 numerals, classify which numeral has the maximum magnitude, evaluated by numeral category: Monetary, Temporal, Percentage, and All.
data_requirements: Publicly available Earnings Conference Calls dataset constructed by Qin and Yang (2019)
S&P 500 companies in U.S. stock exchanges
Financial numerals categorized as Monetary, Temporal, Percentage, and All for magnitude comparison
training_protocol: Adaptive pre-training directly on the magnitude comparison task; hyper-parameters selected by grid search on the validation set. Other executable training details are unknown.
evaluation_protocol: Validation-set evaluation of Magnitude Comparison, reported as accuracy for list maximum from 5 numbers. The broader dataset split is chronological train/validation/test in a 7:1:2 instance ratio, but the reported selected results are validation-set results.
strict_requirements: Use the publicly available Earnings Conference Calls dataset constructed by Qin and Yang (2019).
Evaluate the WWM-BERT+NCC+MC variant on the Magnitude Comparison task.
Use the list maximum from 5 numbers setting.
Report validation-set accuracy separately for Monetary, Temporal, Percentage, and All categories.

This paper describes a numeric-oriented hierarchi- cal transformer model (NumHTML ) to predict stock returns, and ﬁnancial risk using multi-modal aligned earnings calls data by taking advantage of the different categories of num- bers (monetary, temporal, percentages etc.) and their magni- tude.
This dataset contains 576 earning calls recordings, correspond to 88,829 text-audio aligned sentences, for S&P 500 compa- nies in U.S. stock exchanges.
Earnings conference call data, including text and audio, is an important source of unstructured data

Dataset: In line with previous work (Yang et al. 2020; Sawhney et al. 2020) for multi-task ﬁnancial forecasting, in this evaluation, we use a publicly available Earning Confer- ence Calls dataset constructed by Qin and Yang (2019). This dataset contains 576 earning calls recordings, correspond to 88,829 text-audio aligned sentences, for S&P 500 compa- nies in U.S. stock exchanges.

We ﬁnd that the ‘NCC’ task cannot guarantee the accuracy beneﬁts for the maxi- mum list task. However, the adaptive pre-training directly on the magnitude comparison task can signiﬁcantly improve performance (94% vs 88% on average).

To fa- cilitate a direct comparison with the current state-of-the-art (Sawhney et al. 2020), we split the dataset into mutually ex- clusive training/validation/testing sets in the ratio of 7:1:2 (refers to instances) in chronological order, since future data cannot be used for prediction.
To begin with, we present the results on the validation set for the adaptive training used by NumHTML.
